obligations.note: The change adds coapplicant_tax_id (a tax identifier, which ENC-1 names as NPI) to ApplicantFields.ALL but not to NpiRegistry.FIELDS or the approved mortgage.npi_fields. CaseStore.protect only encrypts registry fields, so the value is saved in clear text. The 'exhaustive' ENC-1 control test passes only because it checks the registry's own list, and no exception in the register covers this.

Retention.purge (in RET-1 scope) now explicitly removes coapplicant_tax_id, and RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold passed in CI. That test is a fixed sample, while RET-1 requires exhaustive evidence, and none exists for the changed purge code.

The change names CHG-25867, a standard ticket approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-11, before review. Its components (mortgage.cases, mortgage.retention, mortgage.control-tests) cover all three touched paths.
wen.li@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage and a different person from the author Priya Raman, gave a code_review approval.
Both approvals name the head commit 56dda28, which is the change's only commit.

records/ci/run.json shows success on head 56dda28. The JUnit reports list 124 tests with none skipped or failed, including the registered ENC-1 and RET-1 control tests. I could not rerun locally because the JUnit jar is missing, and the report timestamps and hostname don't match run.json.
ControlFixtures.java is a protected control-test path. rachel.stein (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's lending-eng team) approved the head commit.

summary: The change adds a co-applicant tax identifier to the accepted applicant fields but does not register it as NPI, so CaseStore saves it unencrypted. That violates ENC-1, and no exception covers it. The ENC-1 control test still passes because its domain is the incomplete registry, so it says nothing about the new field. The process records (ticket, independent review, control-owner approval, CI on the head commit) are in order, and RET-1 is open because only sample evidence exists. Because ENC-1 is refuted, the change is rejected.
